statement: GET https://crumblcookies.com/ serves the public home directly (HTTP 200, no redirect) with og:site_name 'Crumbl Cookies' and <html lang="en-US">; the site is Next.js on Vercel behind Cloudflare (x-powered-by: Next.js, x-vercel-id, x-matched-path: /en-US, server: cloudflare).

The home hero is an auto-rotating slick carousel of promotions: 'Back to School Bundl' (Order Now -> /order/carry_out, footnote 'Flavors are subject to change.'), 'Tour of Europe' (video slide, Order Now -> /order), 'Dirty Sodas Are Here!' (Find My Store -> /dirty-sodas), plus cloned slides; the hero is 80svh on a #ffb9cd (--color-primary) background with bottom-left headline/subtitle/CTA and dot indicators.

The 'Weekly Flavors' section (eyebrow pill 'Aug 16 - 22', heading 'Weekly Flavors', sub 'New and returning flavors drop every Monday. Try them before they're gone!') lists six rotating flavors with per-card background colors and images from crumbl.video: Creme Brûlée Cookie (#f3be6b), Cannoli Cookie (#ffe8c2), Chocolate Tiramisu Cake (#7b4c3b), Swedish Candy Cookie ft. BUBS™ (#fea6b5), Vanilla Chocolate Gelato Cookie (#784f3c), Stroopwafel Sandwich Cookie (#d28c48); each card carries a 'This Week Only' badge plus Learn More (profile route) and Order Now (/order) controls.

The 'Classic Flavors' section (eyebrow 'Always Available', sub 'These flavors are here to stay! Enjoy your classic favorites anytime.') lists Pink Sugar Cookie (#ffb9cd) and Chocolate Chip Cookie (#673d28) with Learn More and Order Now controls.

The home page stylesheet defines --color-primary:#ffb9cd, --color-primary-wcag:#f79db7, --color-primary-light:#ffe6e5, --color-dark-blue:#086de7, font-family __CrumblSansFont_61a45f (weights 300/400/700/800) plus Aug-2026 partnership fonts, radius 2xl cards, and hover background #673d28 on flavor cards with inverted (white) text.

The fixed header is transparent over the pink hero (a pink bg-primary layer fades in on scroll), with a hamburger + 'Menu' control on the left, the Crumbl wordmark logo centered, and an 'Order Now' black pill on the right; the mobile drawer contains Home, Order, Locations, Catering, Gift Cards, Merch, Menu, Order Now, Sign in.

The footer has Company (Rewards, Our story, Support, Allergens, Blog, Gift Card Balance), Flavors (Flavor Map, Dirty Sodas, Fan Favorites Vote) and Get Involved (Press, Collaborate, Franchising, Franchise Store Jobs, HQ Careers, Crumbl Cares) columns, social links (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest), '© 2026 all rights reserved.', 'Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors', and legal links (Privacy policy, Terms and Conditions, Gift Card/Voucher Terms, Non-edible Cookie Preferences).

The configuration-scoped anonymous acquisition tool fails closed on the home page because the site's own runtime emits 19 non-GET analytics/telemetry requests (all aborted, none performed); direct Playwright browser capture of the same route/viewport was used instead and succeeded with identical frames across three rapid captures (self-similarity 1.0, calibration status 'calibrated').

In-scope home assets (9 Crumbl Sans/partnership font files, 3 hero images, 9 flavor images including the BUBS partner logo, 5 favicons) were downloaded byte-exact from their source origins (crumblcookies.com, crumbl.video) into source-assets/2026-08-20.crumbl-cookies-r1/ and mirrored byte-identically to clone/static/assets/; the manifest declares 26 required assets, all verified by the static diagnostic section.

Expanded scope recon (2026-08-20): /menu answers the branded 404 anonymously (weekly menu surface lives on home); /profiles/<slug> is a Next.js SSR shell whose full product payload is frozen in __NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.structuredData; /stores SSR-renders the store list; /order is a Delivery/Pickup/gift-card landing; /order/pickup and /order/delivery are client-rendered SPA shells whose pageProps carry allActiveStores (1092) and metroAreas (48).

Each flavor profile page exposes a complete product payload in structuredData: name, description, image, nutrition (calories/fat/cholesterol/sodium/carbs/sugars/protein), allergens, and aggregate rating with review count. Eight profiles (6 weekly + 2 classic) were captured and frozen as the deterministic seed.

The order SPA capture carries allActiveStores (1092) and metroAreas (48); the clone freezes a 6-store deterministic subset spanning TX/SD/OK/GA/AZ/SC with address, hours, phone, sources, and soda flag, per data-reduction rules (entity count only).

The source flavor-profile and order SPA pages are client-rendered (content appears only after API-backed hydration; profile networkidle can time out); the clone renders the same frozen content server-side. Functional comparison flags observable-state differences that are render-timing artifacts, not content divergence: all compared observations still pass their assertions on the source.

Marketing pages (our-story, catering, giftcards, rewards, allergens, dirty-sodas, contact, giftcard-balance, flavor-vote, blog, press, privacy, termsandconditions, digital-giftcard-terms-and-conditions, careers, jobs, collaborate, crumbl-cares, franchising, flavors/secret-menu) are rendered from the captured home/footer copy and the source i18n dictionary; each route renders its own title and body through the shared marketing shell (route handlers bind the loop path via a default argument, so no page leaks another page's content). The login page reproduces the source sign-in form (name + phone + send-code) and drives the local registration/sign-in API. /account answers with the sign-in shell when anonymous and a member page when the local session is authenticated.

The pickup/delivery order flow is a local deterministic SPA: store select -> box build (4/6/12-pack) -> flavor picker -> cart -> contact/pickup-or-delivery details -> review -> simulated payment (websitebench local-sandbox: approved 201 / declined 402 / retryable 402) -> confirmation with order id. Amounts, currency, owner and fingerprint are always server-derived from the validated cart; payment-like client fields are rejected. All five state recipes in scope/verify.json execute in a real browser.

Each flavor profile shows a 'Top reviews' section (title + 'Based on the highest ratings' subtitle) with three real source comments and the 'Tried this cookie? Download the Crumbl App to write a review!' prompt; ratings and review counts are frozen from the profile structuredData for determinism. An 'Add To Favorites' toggle stores local-only state in sessionStorage and never contacts the server.

The clone reproduces the source cookie-consent surface (Accept All / Reject Non-Essential Cookies) as a display-only banner for one session view; no cookie is stored, no analytics or advertising exists, and closing it persists nothing. This mirrors the source surface without any of its tracking effects.

Approved orders return order id + receipt id and enqueue a LOCAL_SIMULATION order-confirmation mail job into the local outbox (template crumbl-cookies.order-confirmation.v1, purpose registered in backend/runtime.json); GET /api/orders/{order_number} returns the placed order. No real email is sent and no provider is contacted.

Modules the source site does not expose were removed: 'View All Flavors' (profile, /menu is 404), 'Back to Home' links (profile/login/marketing — the source relies on header navigation), 'Back to All Stores' (store detail), and the no-results 'View all stores' link. The order landing gained the missing 'Catering' choice to match the source /order page.

The order flow matches source fields: 'Select a tip amount' (0/1/2/3 USD, 100% to bakers) with server-side bound (<= $1000), 'Voucher / Promo Code' with the deterministic local code CRUMBL10 (10% off) and the source-style invalid-code error, and 'Add a note (optional)'. Amounts are server-derived: subtotal minus discount, tax on the discounted subtotal, plus tip.

When authenticated, every page header shows 'Hi, {display_name}' + 'Sign out' (desktop header-actions and mobile drawer), resolved server-side from the HttpOnly session cookie via /api/auth/me and rendered across pages. Sign out revokes the server session and clears the cookie; the login page hides its form and shows 'Welcome back' when already signed in. Invalid phone input shows the source error text and does not navigate.

Full local auth on the vendored LocalAuthStore: /api/auth/begin (phone + name) starts the store's registration OTP flow for new phones or its password-reset OTP flow for existing accounts — the store generates the 6-digit code, persists only salt+hash, and surfaces it as a simulated SMS via LOCAL_ONLY mail (no real SMS/email). /api/auth/verify validates the code in the store (wrong code 422, exhausted attempts locked), then completes registration or password reset and rotates the session into an authenticated HttpOnly cookie (__Host-websitebench-crumbl-cookies-session, Secure, SameSite=Lax — from the runtime session-cookie contract). /api/auth/me resolves the cookie; /account shows a member page when signed in and the sign-in shell otherwise; /api/auth/signout revokes the session. Repeated begins inside the store cooldown answer 429. No real SMS, account, or plaintext credential ever leaves the machine.

Links that would leave the site (merch.crumbl.com, OpenStreetMap copyright, social handles) route to the local /external/<host> boundary page instead of performing any remote request; the route uses {slug:path} so host/path forms like /external/www.openstreetmap.org/copyright resolve (200) alongside plain hosts. Verified: 34 rendered routes return their expected status, zero remote URLs in rendered HTML, CSP script-src 'self' with no inline scripts or handlers.

Every non-API 404 (unknown routes, /menu, unknown profile/store slugs) renders a branded 'Oh no!' page through the shared marketing shell, preserving the full primary navigation (header, mobile menu, footer) per scope journey error-not-found; API 404s stay JSON. Verified in a real browser with zero console errors.
